notes: TBox revision. The rule has no exception for fixed cash flows and a positive yield (price is the present value of the cash flows, decreasing in the discount rate), so the original answers are right; the revision flips the sign, a common confusion and clearly false. Derivability very_unlikely: the rule is stated directly and follows from no subclass chain. The three derived queries apply the rule to bonds of invented issuers (Thornbury Holdings, the town of Elmsworth, the Port of Calderwick) named in the prompt with their class, so the rule is their only route (inheritance, 2 hops, bridge in the prompt). Well-known members such as US Treasuries or the Bund are not asked: their price moves are reported by name daily, which would make the answer depend on storage. The third is an application: whether a holder who bought at issue gains or loses. Migration (2026-11-11): the two indeterminate Treasury and Bund queries and their worlds were dropped (TBox is determinate only); the Spanish question was reworded from a rise-or-fall choice, which two models answered with the first option, to an open question; the conjunction now states the rule in the direct question's plain wording, after three models misread the "raises its price" form; a disjunction was added. Near unrelated: the coupon, a bond term the edit does not touch.
